relevance_note: Case report of a woman with adult-onset Alexander disease: 'Genetic testing identified a heterozygous GFAP c.620A>T (p.Glu207Val) variant', plus her brother and a literature table of Glu207 cases.
method_note: Hand extraction; a short Python script in the scratch directory assembled the JSON from values read by hand and checked spans verbatim. Scope: the index patient (single unnamed patient, label 'patient'), her brother (same GFAP variant), two sisters with suggestive features but no genetic confirmation (labelled in order of mention, aged 68 and 63), two maternal cousins with genetically confirmed AxD, and the five previously published cases in Table 1 rows 1-5 (Table 1 has no label column; row 6 'Current report' is the index patient). Parents and eight other siblings ('remained asymptomatic', untested) get no rows. The 52-year-old male in the Discussion ('previously reported in a 52-year-old male ... [8]') was treated as the same person as Table 1 row 4 (Gass et al., 2017 [8], same variant, onset 52 years). The sisters' features ('vocal cord tremors, unsteady gait, and autonomic dysregulation') are stated jointly for both with 'such as', so they were not assigned to either sister (no phenotype rows; checklist not reported). No variant rows for the maternal cousins: the paper says only 'genetically confirmed AxD' without naming a variant or the gene for them. Brother's variant recorded from 'identical mutation' plus the proband's printed variant; his zygosity and inheritance left not reported. Inheritance for the patient left not reported: maternal carriage is only 'implicated', no parent was tested. In silico predictions (PolyPhen-2, MutationTaster) were not treated as functional evidence. Table 1 rows: gene GFAP taken from the Discussion sentence on residue 207; Table 1 'splice-site' mapped to 'splice'; disease label 'AxD' from the group sentence introducing Table 1. Checklist judgements for the patient: chronic constipation counted as bowel dysfunction (autonomic); rhythmic palatal myoclonus counted as palatal tremor; T2*GRE hypointensity suggesting basal ganglia mineralization counted as basal ganglia abnormality; cerebral white matter abnormality left not reported (only a periventricular rim, 'without deep white matter involvement'); cognitive decline left not reported (mild memory impairment attributed to a stroke 24 years earlier). 'Routine laboratory investigations were unremarkable' is a whole-panel normal result, recorded as written (abnormal routine laboratory investigations, excluded). Age at onset 65 years comes from Table 1 'Current report'. No contradictions found.
